g.text: One neuron, one input, one update rule —
the loop every later model is a scaled-up version of.
1958 — ROSENBLATT · MSE LOSS · SGD UPDATE · LEARNING RATE

div.style: font-size:23px; line-height:1.45; color:#1f1a14; font-style:italic; font-family:Fraunces, Georgia, serif;

foreignObject.div: Training a model is a controlled descent down an error surface. The slope tells you which way is downhill; the learning rate tells you how big a step to take; the loop ends when the slope itself goes to zero — not when the error does.

g.text: Two knobs to learn: m (the weight) and b (the bias). x is given; ŷ is computed.
REPEAT — for every example, every epoch
the gradient magnitude drops below tolerance — ‖∇J‖ < ε. Not when the error itself hits zero (it never does on real data).
The error surface, walked down step by step
Descent on J(w) = w², η = 0.1, start w = 5

div.style: font-size:15px; line-height:1.55; color:#4a4239; font-family:Spectral, Georgia, serif;

foreignObject.div: Each red dot is one gradient-descent step: w ← w − η · 2w. The trajectory bunches as we approach the minimum because the gradient 2w itself shrinks — so the step size shrinks too, without anyone scheduling it.

g.text: η is the single most important hyperparameter

div.style: font-size:15px; line-height:1.55; color:#4a4239; font-family:Spectral, Georgia, serif;

foreignObject.div: Three runs of the same gradient-descent loop on J(w) = w², all starting at w = 5. η = 0.02 converges but crawls. η = 0.10 is the sweet spot for this problem. η = 0.55 overshoots the minimum, lands further from it than before, and oscillates with growing amplitude — divergence. Failure tell: if the loss curve goes up after the first few epochs, cut η by 10×.

g.text: Three lines, four corrections, one loop
m -= η · error · x ; b -= η · error
① Perceptron is from 1958, not 1956 (Rosenblatt, Psychological Review).
② What we derived is linear regression, not Rosenblatt's step-activation perceptron.
③ Stop on gradient ≈ 0, not error = 0 (real-data MSE never hits zero).
④ Multi-feature form has one shared bias b, not one per feature.
Same loop. Same stopping rule. Bigger surface.
Drawn computationally — every dot in §03 and §04 is one real iteration of w ← w − η·2w.
